title: AI Packaging Design Generator | AIVideosUGC
description: Create studio-style packaging designs in minutes. Upload one product photo, describe the look in one line, and download a realistic mockup for your listing.
lead: Upload one product photo and describe the pack you want. You get a realistic packaging design, with a new background and style, ready for the listing.

steps.d: Upload a clear photo of the product you sell. A sharp photo gives you a better design.
Name the look in one line, such as a gold cosmetic pack or a plain kraft box. The picture comes back in minutes.
Review the design, tweak the line if you need to, and download a sharp file for the listing.

steps_h2: How to Make a Packaging Design in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: A clear product photo starts it. You leave with a packaging design the listing can use.

faq.q: What does a packaging design tool make?
faq.a: It makes a packaging picture from one product photo. You name the style, then download a file you can check before anything is printed.

faq.q: Do I need to know design first?
faq.a: No. You do not need a design job or a design degree. Upload the photo and name the look in plain words.

faq.q: How does a packaging design get made?
faq.a: Upload a photo of the box, pouch, or bottle, then name the style in one sentence. Download the square file when the shape matches the product you ship.

faq.q: Can my shop put this on a listing?
faq.a: Yes. Use the design as the listing image or on the product page. Check the shape against the real pack before you publish it.

faq.q: How soon is the pack design ready?
faq.a: The preview comes back in the same sitting, so you are not booking a designer for that file. If a color is off, edit the line and run it again.

faq.q: Can I make a design for each product I sell?
faq.a: Yes. Run each product from its own photo and a new style line. You download a square design for each listing.

faq.q: Can I start from the listing photo I already have?
faq.a: Yes. The product photo already on the listing is the right start. You can add more reference photos when a close detail matters.

faq.q: Where can I post the finished design?
faq.a: Use the square design on the listing and the product page. A tall, square, or wide crop can go to the feed that needs it.

faq.q: What do I pay before I download?
faq.a: You pay with a plan, not a design invoice. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A photo is 24 credits, shown before it runs. A failed job puts those credits back.

faq.q: Can I use the design in an ad or send it to a client?
faq.a: Yes. Use it on your listing, in a paid ad, or hand the file to a client whose product is in the photo. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: Can I describe the style instead of drawing it?
faq.a: Yes. Say the style in one line instead of building the pack in design software. A new product can keep the same kind of file.

reviews.h2: How Shops Preview a Pack on a Shelf
reviews.lead: Example shelf scenes, from a coffee pack to a pouch. This is not a check of print color or the small legal words.

items.t: A finished shelf frame from one pack photo
items.d: Example: a coffee shop uploads the bag and gets a square cafe scene to judge before a print order.

items.t: The mockup and a clip in one project
items.d: Example: a tea shop makes the tin picture and a short product clip together, in one project, without a second app.

items.t: Start from the bottle photo or the link
items.d: Example: a sauce shop pastes the product page link, or uploads the bottle, and the preview keeps that bottle's shape.

items.t: An AI actor and captions on the clip
items.d: Example: the pouch stays the shelf picture. On the video, the shop picks an AI actor, a generated person, then adds words on screen.

items.t: The same jar scene in another language
items.d: Example: the wood-shelf still stays as it is, and the spoken line on the clip is recorded again for a second market.

items.t: A voiceover and a track on the clip
items.d: Example: the carton preview is for slides you show a store buyer. On the video, the editor adds a spoken voice and a track from the music library.

items.t: An AI actor instead of a filmed spot
items.d: Example: a supplement shop uses an AI actor, a generated person, to hold the pack. Small ingredient text can blur, so the real label photo keeps the wording.

items.t: A digital twin for the next bag
items.d: Example: a pet-food shop uses a digital twin, the same generated person, so the next bag clip matches the first. No new light setup.

items.t: A script, then a second version
items.d: Example: a juice shop pastes the product link, takes a short script, and compares two bottle versions in the same scene.

items.t: Publish the clip, or start from the API
items.d: Example: after a look at the sample print, the shop posts the clip to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram). The API lets the product list start the next box.

more_sections.h2: What You Can Do With the Pack Design
more_sections.lead: Upload a product photo and name the style in one line. A voice and an actor stay available if that design also becomes a video.

items.d: The packaging design is a still. Add a voiceover or captions, plus a track from the music library, only when that still also becomes a clip.

items.t: An AI Actor on the Later Clip
items.d: The design shows the pack you uploaded. An AI actor can hold it in a later clip, and that face can return for the next product.

items.t: A Style Line, Not a Drawing
items.d: Name the pack style in a short line, such as a matte box and a cream label. Or paste the product page and start from the product shown there.
Make a second style of the same box and keep the one that fits the listing. Each photo is 24 credits, shown before it runs.
Download the square design, then use the editor if a color note is off. A clip of that pack can still go to TikTok, and the file has no watermark.
Write the style line in the language the listing needs. Speak it only if you also make a clip.
